## TL;DR

I closed the Settings QA coverage gap with scratch-only browser runs, updated the QA record with per-tab outcomes and limits, and fixed a real cross-process worktree-lock race reported by remote validation. I also isolated the servers-command unit tests from live tailnet HTTP discovery after the remote gate exposed environment-dependent results. The Settings audit passed 115 schema-backed controls, plus the hand-rendered and local controls noted below. The focused test files passed locally, and the final scoped RepoOS check passed on the remote runner and locally.

## Work and rationale

Review round 5 found that the original 115-control matrix covered General and Advanced but did not individually audit the other Settings tabs. It also marked the evidence image and engineering report stale for the reviewed tree. I expanded the audit rather than treating the earlier representative save as proof. The General and Advanced run used an in-process auth-less server rooted at `.repoos/qa-1179-control-audit-root`, with a scratch `repoos.toml`. It edited each schema-backed row, checked the server value, reloaded, and compared the restored control. All 115 passed: 91 General and 24 Advanced. It exercised invalid values where controls have a meaningful validation rule and checked that rejected inputs did not replace the saved value.

The schema-row inventory also misses hand-rendered controls. I added scratch round-trips for the General theme selection/favorite, floating-agent visibility, glide and keyboard preferences, activity animation motion/style/size/concurrency, and attachment storage provider. The attachment provider was returned to local after testing. The CTO action checklist was included in the schema matrix and its unknown-ID rejection remains covered by its test.

I ran a second scratch browser pass across the remaining tabs. Notifications' ntfy enable/topic, Telegram toggle, spend threshold, sound, and 24 event preferences saved and restored; a negative spend threshold showed the validation error and kept the previous value. I did not toggle browser push because that would prompt for OS permission. Security's voice provider and session duration round-tripped; enabling authentication without a configured login provider displayed the provider-required error and remained disabled after reload. The voice API key was left blank, and user-management or invite operations were not tested in an auth-less run. Import/Export's five section switches, download, invalid-file message, and valid import were exercised using scratch data. Support's report type, manual draft, and screenshot add/remove were checked, and a support bundle was created under the scratch root. I did not send report notes to an AI agent or open GitHub/file-browser actions. The raw TOML editor saved a scratch change, restored it after reload, and rejected malformed TOML without losing the valid version.

The queued remote check failure named `ensureWorktree resilience > serializes concurrent starts from separate processes on one branch`. The failure exposed a lock initialization race: creating the lock directory and writing its pid are separate filesystem operations. A contender could observe the new directory before `pid` existed, classify it as stale, remove it, and enter the critical section concurrently. I changed stale detection so a missing or invalid pid is treated as a live initialization window until the lock directory exceeds its stale age. A new deterministic subprocess regression pre-creates that empty window, confirms the worktree is not created while it is held, then removes the lock so the operation can complete. The entire resilience test file passed locally.

A later remote gate run failed three `servers-command.test.ts` assertions only on the Tailscale-enabled runner. Reproduction locally showed the same cause: fake status and SSH functions did not replace the default peer HTTP discovery, allowing live services from the actual tailnet into mocked results. I added a shared null HTTP-discovery seam to the SSH/fallback unit cases; the focused suite then passed all 15 tests. Production discovery remains unchanged. The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` then passed: remote build and changed-path tests completed, followed by local format, lint, build, contrast, UI smoke, and guards.

## Approaches tried

I first ran the reported concurrent-start case locally; it passed, so I did not treat the remote-only failure as disproved. I inspected the cross-process lock lifecycle and added a test for the exact mkdir-before-pid interval rather than increasing sleeps in the existing concurrency test. This addressed the race class directly while preserving the old-lock cleanup behavior.

For QA, I kept mutations on the scratch server and left the worktree's project config untouched. The audit separates actual saves and reloads from controls that ask for permissions, credentials, external delivery, or provider calls. The existing Agents visit remained read-only for real project state; a scratch-only custom role was created, reloaded, and removed.

## Challenges and blockers

The Settings page contains schema rows, local browser preferences, special forms, and actions with different persistence semantics. Treating every button as a setting would misstate behavior: import selections are temporary until export, support report drafts are transient, and notification preferences live in browser storage. The QA note records those distinctions and only calls a control persistent when that behavior was observed.

Several live integrations require external proof that was not available in this run. Browser push permission was not requested; no voice key was entered; authentication could not be enabled without a login provider; authenticated user management, email/Telegram invites, AI report generation, GitHub submission, and external notification delivery remain unverified. Runner provisioning, local service installation, and cloud publishing controls were not activated. These limits are stated in the QA record without claiming success.

## Key learnings

Control inventories built only from `data-config-key` omit hand-rendered UI controls. A complete QA pass needs to inventory each active tab panel and classify its controls by persistence and side effect. For cross-process locks, atomic directory creation protects acquisition only after the owner finishes initialization; contenders must not delete a newly created lock just because its owner metadata is not written yet. Regression coverage should model that exact window, not rely solely on a parallel test that may miss it.
